p1s.what: The exclusion of the correction register from the claim-coverage census is correct but is not encoded anywhere as a deliberate, defended decision, unlike test_the_census_reads_every_publication_endpoint.py's NOT_ENDPOINTS list, which asserts by name that specific documents must NOT be swept in. Nothing here asserts the register must stay out, or says why. A future session could 'fix' this by reflex (adding the register to PAPERS thinking it's an oversight) without seeing the reasoning that keeps it out today. This is the CYC-0020 open question, genuinely undecided as a matter of committed record even though the right answer (no) is clear on inspection.

p1s.where: Section 3.1, main manuscript: "The direction is consistent across two cohorts, two drugs and five years of accrual (July 2011 – January 2017)."
p1s.what: The end date (January 2017) is traceable elsewhere in the document to the pazopanib trial's enrolment close (Section 4.11), but the start date, July 2011, appears nowhere else in either document and carries no citation, artifact pointer, or 'read from' note — unlike essentially every other date, count, and quote in this manuscript. Sits awkwardly next to Section 4.11's explicit refusal to state a diagnosis or accrual period it cannot source. Not decision-relevant to any interval or gap in the paper, so it would not mislead a reader about the central claim, but it is the one place in the document where a specific factual claim escapes the sourcing discipline applied everywhere else, and no instrument covers inline accrual-window prose of this kind.

p1s.where: §6, falsifier #5 ("Reconciling the two would take 19 further TAF15 patients with zero deaths — a total TAF15 denominator of 34, more than twice the pooled experience assembled here"); mirrored in emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json -> what_could_kill_this[4]
p1s.what: Round 8's whole point for R7-B4 was to DERIVE the falsifier threshold with zero_death_patients_to_reconcile() instead of asserting it, and this was re-run and independently reproduces 19/34/31.8%/30.4%/20.8% exactly from the committed COHORTS counts, so the numbers are correct today. But test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py (the quantity guard) and mutate_fusion_partner_guard.py (the mutation harness) only bind/mutate the two projected percentages (31.8%/30.4%) and the comparator's 20.8% upper bound — grepped both files for '19 further', 'denominator of 34', 'total_taf15_denominator_required', 'further_zero_death_taf15_patients_required' and 'twice' and found zero matches. The '19', the '34' and the 'more than twice' relation — which are the actual headline output of the function round 8 built specifically so this class of number would never be typed by hand again — have no binding and no mutation, so a future correction to the TAF15 death arm's denominator/events or the comparator's counts could silently desync these three figures from the prose while every existing test stays green.
p1s.class_of_surface_unwatched: a derived quantity with a sibling quantity in the same sentence that IS bound — the guard covers the percentages next to it but not the integer counts, the exact one-of-a-pair shape (A19/A20, A24, A31) this paper's own correction history repeatedly names as its recurring failure mode

p1s.where: §6 falsifier #5 ("a total TAF15 denominator of 34") and §3.3's follow-up caveat, cross-checked against the artifact's `zero_death_patients_to_reconcile()` docstring and `follow_up_warning` field
p1s.what: The falsifier's derivation (comparator arm's Wilson upper bound, 20.8%, held fixed while only the TAF15 arm's denominator grows) is a sound and appropriately self-critical choice — independently recomputed (7/(15+n) crosses 20.79% at n=19, giving denom=34; Fisher exact on 7/34 vs 6/58 gives p=0.219) — but the manuscript's own prose never states why the upper bound rather than the comparator's point estimate (10.3%) is the reconciliation target, or why the comparator is held fixed rather than allowed to grow. That reasoning exists only in the generator's docstring, not in §6. A future editor who 'simplifies' the target to the comparator's point estimate (which would roughly double the threshold to ~68) would silently change what the falsifier means, and nothing in the prose would flag that as a substantive edit. Recommend importing one sentence of the generator's rationale into §6 itself.

p1s.where: §4.7 ("Huang 2023 also reports outcome only for the 53 of 58 patients with follow-up available, and the five without are in neither numerator nor denominator") vs. §3.2/§3.3 ("50 partner-assigned with follow-up")
p1s.what: 53 and 50 look like the same quantity but are not, and the manuscript never bridges them. The artifact resolves it cleanly (of the 53 Huang patients with follow-up, 3 are TCF12/partner-unidentified and are excluded from the two-arm outcome pool, leaving 50), but that second exclusion step is stated nowhere in the manuscript prose — §4.7 attributes the entire 58→53 gap to missing follow-up and is silent on the further 53→50 step. A reader checking the arithmetic from the manuscript text alone (58 − 5 = 53 ≠ 50) will see an apparent inconsistency between two 'load one home' numbers that in fact nest correctly. Recommend one clause in §4.7 naming the 3 TCF12/unassigned patients as the reason 50, not 53, enters the pooled table.

p1s.where: artifact emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning: "The recurrence comparison is confounded the same way, in a direction this record cannot sign"
p1s.what: This artifact field generalizes the death-endpoint reasoning (follow-up truncates at death, so the higher-mortality arm's shorter mean follow-up is partly an artefact of its own event count) to the recurrence/metastasis rows by asserting they are 'confounded the same way'. Not quite true: for recurrence/metastasis the more relevant mechanism is competing-risks informative censoring, which would tend to bias the TAF15 arm's rate DOWNWARD if anything, not merely 'unsigned'. The manuscript's own §3.3 prose is actually more careful than the artifact here (it says only 'not independent of the endpoint being compared'), so this is not currently a defect in the reviewed prose, but it is a latent one: the artifact field is the more likely template a future edit copies verbatim, and if pulled into the manuscript unedited it would overstate a mechanistic equivalence between two genuinely different biases.
